newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Indian Ocean states launch regional group.
newsitem.headline: Indian Ocean states launch regional group.

text.p: Ministers from 14 states meeting in Mauritius have launched the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation (IOR-ARC) to boost trade cooperation, officials said on Friday.
"We have started something big.," Mauritian Foreign Affairs Minister Paul Berenger told reporters. The ministers adopted the new association's charter at the close of a two-day meeting on Thursday.

The IOR-ARC groups Australia, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Madagascar, Malaysia, Mauritius, Mozambique, Oman, Singapore, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania and Yemen to increase cooperation in investment, infrastructure, tourism, science, technology and human resource development as well as trade.
The IOR-ARC charter saw regional trade as a top objective and hoped to achieve it by promoting liberalisation, removing impediments to trade and lowering tariff barriers.

"The focus of the IOR-ARC will have to be cooperation which helps generate productive employment, effects transfer of knowledge and technology, develops human capital and contributes to the individual and collective well-being of the Rim countries," Indian External Affairs Minister Shri Gujral said.
The ministers adopted a work programme focused on promoting investment, trade and technology enhancement.

The meeting set up a mechanism to steer activities until a secretariat is established for the new association. Diplomats said a secretariat was seen by some members of the 14-nation association as premature.
They also said the bid by Mauritius to host the secretariat had been opposed on Tuesday by Australia, backed by South Africa and Singapore.

"In 1993, the Indian Ocean region accounted for 31 percent of the world's population, but 6.3 percent of its GDP (gross domestic product) and 10.7 percent of its trade. In 1994, intra-IOR trade was only 22 percent of the total," Mauritian Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam said on Wednesday.
"There is huge scope for us to do better. The opportunities are immense and our association is long overdue," he added.
